purpose: Normalized Bank for International Settlements foundation for international banking positions and debt securities. Keeps residence, nationality, issuer, counterparty, currency, sector, maturity, valuation and market dimensions explicit so banking claims and bond obligations can later become directed World Map relations.
source_boundary: BIS statistics describe financial positions and securities. They do not establish political control, sovereignty, Axis membership or ultimate beneficial ownership unless the underlying dataset explicitly identifies it.

lbs.coverage_note: Captures around 95% of global cross-border banking activity according to BIS.
primary_questions: Where is the banking position booked?
Which country or sector is the counterparty resident in?
Is the position a claim or liability?
What instrument and currency is involved?
What is the exchange-rate- and break-adjusted quarterly change?
lbs.map_role: Directed cross-border bank claim/liability edges by reporting location and counterparty residence.

cbs.consolidation: consolidated worldwide group; intragroup positions excluded
primary_questions: Which national banking groups carry the exposure?
Which counterparty country bears the immediate exposure?
How does exposure change after guarantees or risk transfers?
What sector and remaining maturity make up the foreign claim?
What derivatives, guarantees and credit commitments sit outside claims?
cbs.map_role: Country-risk exposure from banking-group nationality to counterparty country.

dss.valuation_note: Valuation can differ across countries; retain market/nominal/face-value metadata and never aggregate incompatible valuations without harmonisation.
primary_questions: How much tradable debt is outstanding?
Is it domestic or international market debt?
What currency, maturity and interest-rate structure does it have?
Where available, which holder sector holds it?
dss.map_role: Country/sector bond-market stocks and comparable maturity/currency overlays.

ids.market_scope: securities issued outside the local market of the issuer's residence
ids.compiled_from: security-by-security commercial-source database aggregated by BIS
ids.holder_limitation: IDS does not identify holders of outstanding securities.
ids.map_role: International bond issuance/exposure characteristics. It can identify the debtor/issuer and instrument structure, not the creditor/holder.

observation_schema.rule: Absent dimensions remain null/unknown. A value is not promoted into a bilateral map edge unless reporting/issuer side, counterparty/holder side, direction, period, unit and semantic basis are explicit.

latest_global_observations.notes: All reporting banking offices, all sectors, all instruments. Residence basis; unconsolidated and including intragroup positions.
All reporting banking offices, all sectors, all instruments. This is a banking liability aggregate, not sovereign external debt.
BIS commentary reports outstanding cross-border bank credit of $39.5 trillion at end-Q1 2026. It rose by $1.7 trillion during the quarter.
All bank nationalities. Nationality/consolidated basis; foreign claims are the BIS benchmark CBS measure.

latest_global_observations.maturity: up to and including one year

latest_global_observations.remaining_maturity: up to and including one year

normalization_targets: map BIS country codes to canonical ISO3 only through an explicit crosswalk
keep immediate-counterparty and guarantor bases separate
keep stock and adjusted-change measures separate
keep domestic and international securities markets separate

north_axis_query_plan.boundary: These are empirical BIS facts filtered through a project-defined country set. The filter does not alter legal ownership, debtor/creditor status or political authority.
queries: Cross-border claims of banking offices located in North jurisdictions on residents inside versus outside North.
Cross-border liabilities of North residents to banking offices inside versus outside North.
Foreign claims of banking groups headquartered in North jurisdictions by counterparty country and sector.
Risk-transfer differences between immediate-counterparty and guarantor basis for North banking groups.
Total, domestic and international debt securities of North issuers by government, bank and corporate sector.
North international bond issuance by EUR, USD, DKK, NOK, SEK, GBP, CAD and other currencies.
North maturity wall: securities with remaining maturity up to one year versus longer maturities.
Distinguish issuer-side bond exposure from actual holder-side creditor data; IDS alone cannot answer who owns the bond.

map_projection_rules: LBS bilateral edges render from reporting banking location to counterparty residence, with claim/liability direction labeled.
CBS edges render from banking-group parent nationality to counterparty country and must state immediate-counterparty or guarantor basis.
DSS normally renders as issuer-country/sector scalar or category layers; holder edges only where the relevant holdings table identifies a holder sector.
IDS renders issuer-side international bond structure and never fabricates a holder endpoint.
Flows use adjusted changes only when the BIS measure explicitly reports/derives an adjusted change; stocks are not animated as flows.
Do not combine LBS and CBS values as if they were additive because the consolidation and geography bases differ.

source_layers.title: LBS A6.2 — cross-border positions by counterparty country and reporting-bank location
CBS B2 — foreign claims, immediate counterparty basis
IDS C3 — international debt securities issues and amounts outstanding
International banking statistics and global liquidity indicators at end-March 2026
